channel.title: OpticQuiz Learn
channel.description: Plain-English guides to vision, eye tests, and how they work.

item.title: How Accurate Are Online Color Blindness Tests?
item.description: The calibration problem: why an uncalibrated screen is the real limit on online color tests, what makes one trustworthy, and why you can pass one site and fail another.

item.title: Which Color Vision Test Is Most Accurate?
item.description: Ishihara vs the Farnsworth D-15 vs the anomaloscope vs online tests — what each color vision test is for and which is the clinical gold standard.

item.title: Color Blindness in Kids: How to Test a Child
item.description: How to test a young child for color blindness using shapes instead of numbers, the signs, what age to test, and how it affects school.

item.title: Are Online Vision Tests Worth It? An Honest Comparison
item.description: A verified, fair comparison of the major online vision tests — ZEISS, ACUVUE, Warby Parker, and OpticQuiz — what each does, whether it's really free, and the catch.

item.title: Is Blue Light Bad for Your Eyes? The Honest Answer
item.description: Screen blue light doesn't damage your eyes, and blue-light glasses aren't proven to help. Here's what really causes eye strain.

item.title: Am I Colorblind? Signs and How to Check
item.description: Am I colorblind? Common signs include confusing reds, greens and browns, muddy traffic lights, and not seeing numbers others see in dot images. Take a free color vision test to check.

item.title: Can Color Blindness Be Cured or Corrected?
item.description: Can color blindness be cured? Inherited color blindness is permanent and cannot be cured. Color-boosting glasses help some people tell confusing colors apart but don't restore normal vision.

item.title: What Does a Dominant Eye Mean?
item.description: Your dominant eye is the one your brain favors for aiming and judging direction, like handedness. About two-thirds of people are right-eye dominant. Find yours with a quick guided test.

item.title: How to Test for Astigmatism at Home
item.description: To check for astigmatism at home, view a fan of radial lines: if some directions look darker or sharper than others, it suggests astigmatism. It can hint but can't measure your prescription.

item.title: What Is the Eye's Blind Spot?
item.description: The eye's blind spot is a small area of the retina where the optic nerve exits, with no light receptors, so images there aren't seen. Everyone has one; the brain fills the gap. Find yours.

item.title: How Far Should You Sit From Your Screen?
item.description: Sit about an arm's length (50-70 cm) from a monitor with the top at or just below eye level, and follow the 20-20-20 rule to ease eye strain. Viewing distance also affects on-screen vision tests.

item.title: Why Is My Night Vision Getting Worse?
item.description: Trouble seeing at night or in fog is often a contrast-sensitivity issue rather than sharpness, and can come with age, cataracts, or dry eye. Learn what to check and test your contrast.

item.title: Color Blindness, Explained — Types, Causes, and What It's Like
item.description: Color blindness explained in plain English: the types (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia), what causes it, how common it is, and how it looks in daily life. Test your color vision free.

item.title: How Ishihara Plates Work — The Hidden-Number Test Explained
item.description: How Ishihara plates work: why a hidden number appears or vanishes in a field of colored dots, the different plate designs, and what an online plate test can and cannot tell you.

item.title: What 20/20 Vision Actually Means
item.description: What 20/20 vision actually means: Snellen fractions decoded, why 20/20 isn't perfect vision, what 20/40 or 20/15 mean, and whether you can test visual acuity accurately on a screen.

item.title: Contrast Sensitivity vs. Sharpness — The Other Axis of Vision
item.description: Contrast sensitivity vs visual acuity: why you can have 20/20 and still struggle in fog, glare, and dim light, what contrast sensitivity measures, and why it can change first.

item.title: Vision & Eye Test Glossary — OpticQuiz
item.description: A plain-English glossary of vision and eye-test terms: visual acuity, Snellen, logMAR, contrast sensitivity, JND, Ishihara, protan/deutan/tritan, anomaloscope, hyperacuity, flicker fusion, and more.
